findings.description: publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS MySQL instance directly to the internet and drastically increasing attack surface for a data store holding credentials and application data that should only be reachable from within the VPC.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the database storage and any automated backups/snapshots are not encrypted at rest, violating data protection requirements.

The master username is hard-coded to 'admin' and the password is sourced from a variable with no secrets-manager integration or rotation; this password is also propagated in plaintext into the EC2 instance's user_data, and combined with publicly_accessible=true this makes credential-based compromise significantly more likely.

The EC2 instance's user_data script embeds the database username and password in cleartext, both in the launch configuration (retrievable via the EC2 metadata service/API) and written out to a PHP file on disk, risking credential disclosure to anyone with instance or API access.

The policy grants wildcard actions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on all resources (Resource: "*") to the EC2 instance role, violating least privilege; because this role is attached to a network-facing, publicly reachable instance, compromise of the instance would enable broad lateral movement and control over S3, EC2, and RDS resources.

The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, providing no network egress restriction and enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control communication if the database or an associated instance is compromised.
